text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000113 bills 99215 well above its risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity band, including on low-complexity patients, but documentation is too thin to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevated 99215 rate is not explained by panel acuity alone: the by-complexity table shows this provider roughly double the all-provider 99215 share in each band from 0 to 4 conditions. A third of its 99215s fall on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions, and sampled examples such as C0055397, C0055603 and C0056336 (acute upper respiratory infection, no chronic conditions) and C0054718 and C0056027 (follow-up visit codes) are the kind of encounters that rarely support high-complexity MDM. Against that, the sampled high-complexity 99215s (e.g., C0054914, C0056072) look plausible. The few records returned show no unsupported levels and no cloned-data signal, but only 2 of them are documented 99215s, so they cannot tip the balance either way. A reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet, prioritising the acute-only and Z09 visits, and check whether the MDM or time documented there supports level 5."}
